### Identification

Once we have specified the hypothetical quantities from our thought experiment, we "identify" them, meaning write them in terms of the observed rather than counterfactual data. It is sufficient to identify the quantity:


::: aside
**Notes on identification** 

**A**. In the first line, we use the law of iterated expectations.

**B**. In the second line, we use the definition for counterfactual outcome $Y_i^{(a)}$ as specified in @eq-independence-swig.

**C**. In the third line, we use the fact that when $L_i$ is fixed, $f_{Y}(U_{Y_i} , L_i, a)$ is a function of random variable $U_{Y_i}$ and $A_i$ is a function of $U_{A_i}$. Since $U_{Y_i}$ and $U_{A_i}$ are independent by definition of the NPSEM-IE, $f_{Y}(U_{Y_i} , L_i, a) \perp A_i | L_i$.

**D**. In the fourth line we consider the expected value of $f_{Y}(U_{Y_i} , L_i, a)$ when $A_i = a$, in particular

**E**. In the fifth line, we use the definition for observed value $Y_i$ according as specified in @eq-independence-dag.

:::

$$
\begin{aligned}
 \frac{1}{n} \sum_i E[Y_i^{(a)}]                    &= E \left[ \frac{1}{n} \sum_i E[Y_i^{(a)} | L_i] \right] \\
                                                    &= E \left[ \frac{1}{n} \sum_i E[f_{Y}(U_{Y_i} , L_i, a) | L_i] \right] \\
                                                    &= E \left[ \frac{1}{n} \sum_i E[f_{Y}(U_{Y_i} , L_i, a) | L_i , A_i] \right] \\
                                                    &= E \left[ \frac{1}{n} \sum_i E[f_{Y}(U_{Y_i} , L_i, a) | L_i , A_i = a] \right] \\
                                                    &= E \left[ \frac{1}{n} \sum_i E[Y_i | L_i , A_i = a] \right] \\
\end{aligned}
$$
